verdict.rationale: Foreloop documents a single approval gate — "Nothing runs until a person approves a contract" and "Decisions that need a human land in one approvals list" — which gives an engineering-lead a binary human-in-the-loop checkpoint before an agent's work proceeds. But there is no evidence of configurable tiered autonomy levels (e.g., auto-approving low-risk tasks while gating high-risk ones); it's a uniform approval step, not a tiered permission system. Missing for 10: documented tiers/levels of autonomy, configurable thresholds per task risk, any settings distinguishing what an agent can do unsupervised vs. what requires confirmation.
